newsitem.title: USA: Two die in New Year gunfire celebrations in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Two die in New Year gunfire celebrations in Texas.

text.p: A man accidentally shot and killed his 7-year-old daughter when he fired a gun to celebrate the New Year, police said on Wednesday.
Another 39-year-old man was killed at a party when a number of people went outside to shoot their guns off at midnight, said Harris County Sheriff's Department Detective Ben Beall.

The shootings occurred despite a police bid to discourage people from greeting the New Year with gunfire. In recent days, television stations ran public service advertisements pointing out the dangers of firing pistols into the air.
"They've (the public) got this thing about getting out their guns. They get out there and start shooting straight up into the air and have no idea where the bullet is going," Beall said.
The girl died when her father, Randy Farmer, fired a bullet into their home as he stood in the front yard and tried to unjam his .380-calibre pistol, Beall said.

Emergency crews took the girl, Mary Farmer, to hospital, but she was dead on arrival from a gunshot wound to the chest, Beall said. Her father was in Harris County Jail on charges of criminally negligent homicide, he said.

In the other incident, Edward Titus died when he was shot by friend Hugh Watson. Watson's handgun accidentally went off as he reloaded after firing off several rounds to celebrate the arrival of 1997, Beall said. The two men were part of a group who were outside blasting away shortly after midnight, he said.
Watson, who wounded his own finger in the shooting, had not yet been charged, but the case would be sent to the grand jury for consideration, Beall said.
